title: STL Mastery
description: Master the C++ STL from containers and iterators to algorithms and custom comparators, with DSA problems in every lesson.

lessons.title: 001. What is STL
lessons.notes:
STL = Standard Template Library.
Four parts: containers, iterators, algorithms, functors.
Containers store data, algorithms work on data, iterators connect the two.
Header: #include <bits/stdc++.h> (practice) or specific headers.

logic.problem: Why use STL instead of writing my own structures?
logic.thinking: Tested, fast code saves contest and interview time.
logic.logic: Algorithms work on any container through iterators.
logic.approach:
1. Pick the container.
2. Use iterators to point at data.
3. Call an algorithm.
logic.code:
vector<int> v = {3, 1, 2};
sort(v.begin(), v.end());

lessons.title: 002. Templates and Generic Programming Basics
lessons.notes:
template<typename T> makes one function work for many types.
The compiler creates a version for each type you use.
STL containers are class templates: vector<int>, map<string, int>.
Template errors are long; read the first line.

logic.problem: Write one swap that works for int, double and string.
logic.thinking: The logic is the same for every type.
logic.logic: Replace the type with T.
logic.approach:
1. Write the function with T.
2. Call it with any type.
3. Let the compiler deduce T.
logic.code:
template <typename T>
void mySwap(T& a, T& b) { T t = a; a = b; b = t; }

lessons.title: 003. Iterators
lessons.notes:
An iterator is a pointer-like handle to an element.
begin() = first element, end() = one past the last.
Types: input, output, forward, bidirectional, random access.
Useful: advance, distance, next, prev, rbegin/rend.

logic.problem: Walk a container without caring whether it is a vector or a list.
logic.thinking: Iterators give one interface for every container.
logic.logic: Move with ++, read with *.
logic.approach:
1. it = c.begin().
2. While it != c.end().
3. Use *it, then ++it.
logic.code:
for (auto it = v.begin(); it != v.end(); ++it) cout << *it << " ";
auto last = prev(v.end());

lessons.title: 004. STL Complexity Cheat Sheet
lessons.notes:
vector: access O(1), push_back O(1) amortised, insert/erase in the middle O(n).
deque: both ends O(1).
list: insert/erase O(1) with an iterator, no random access.
set/map: O(log n). unordered_set/map: O(1) average, O(n) worst.
priority_queue: push/pop O(log n), top O(1).
sort O(n log n), binary_search O(log n).

logic.problem: Which container is fast enough for n = 1e5?
logic.thinking: Read the cost of each operation before choosing.
logic.logic: Match the most frequent operation to a cheap container.
logic.approach:
1. List your operations.
2. Check the table.
3. Choose the cheapest fit.

lessons.title: 005. Modern C++ Tools for STL
lessons.notes:
auto deduces the type.
Range-for: for (auto& x : v).
Structured bindings: for (auto& [k, v] : m).
Lambdas: [](int a, int b){ return a < b; }.
Brace init: vector<int> v = {1, 2, 3};

logic.problem: Loop over a map without writing iterators.
logic.thinking: Modern syntax removes boilerplate.
logic.logic: Use auto& to avoid copies.
logic.approach:
1. for (auto& [k, v] : m).
2. Use k and v directly.
logic.code:
map<string,int> m = {{"a", 1}, {"b", 2}};
for (auto& [k, v] : m) cout << k << " " << v << "\n";

lessons.title: 006. vector Basics
lessons.notes:
vector<int> v; v(n), v(n, x), v = {1, 2, 3}.
push_back, pop_back, size, empty, back, front, clear.
Index with v[i] or v.at(i) (checks bounds).
Pass big vectors by const reference.

logic.problem: Store input whose size is known only at run time.
logic.thinking: A dynamic array grows automatically.
logic.logic: Use vector as the default array.
logic.approach:
1. Read n.
2. vector<int> v(n).
3. Fill and use.

lessons.title: 007. vector Advanced
lessons.notes:
capacity vs size; reserve(n) avoids reallocations.
emplace_back builds in place.
insert(pos, x), erase(pos), erase(first, last).
2D: vector<vector<int>> g(r, vector<int>(c, 0)).
assign, resize, swap, shrink_to_fit.

logic.problem: Create a grid with r rows and c columns filled with 0.
logic.thinking: Each row is its own vector.
logic.logic: Create rows with a fill value.
logic.approach:
1. g(r, vector<int>(c, 0)).
2. Access g[i][j].

lessons.title: 008. array and C-style Arrays
lessons.notes:
array<int, 5> a: fixed size, on the stack, knows its size().
Supports begin(), end(), fill, and works with algorithms.
Global C arrays start at 0; locals do not.
Use vector when the size is not known at compile time.

logic.problem: Store 26 letter counts with fixed size.
logic.thinking: The size never changes.
logic.logic: Use array when the size is a compile-time constant.
logic.approach:
1. array<int, 26> cnt{}.
2. cnt[c - 'a']++.
logic.code:
array<int, 26> cnt{};
for (char c : s) cnt[c - 'a']++;

lessons.title: 009. string Methods
lessons.notes:
size, empty, push_back, pop_back, substr(pos, len), find, rfind, erase, insert, replace.
s.find returns string::npos when not found.
Compare with ==, <, >; concatenate with +.
Sort letters: sort(s.begin(), s.end()).

logic.problem: Check if a word contains a pattern.
logic.thinking: find tells where, npos tells not found.
logic.logic: Compare the result with npos.
logic.approach:
1. pos = s.find(p).
2. If pos != npos, found at pos.

lessons.title: 010. String Utilities
lessons.notes:
stoi, stoll, stod: string to number. to_string: number to string.
stringstream splits and parses text.
getline(cin, s) reads a line; getline(ss, tok, ',') splits by a character.
string_view is a light read-only view (C++17).

logic.problem: Split "1.2.3" into numbers.
logic.thinking: A stream can read pieces separated by a delimiter.
logic.logic: getline with a delimiter.
logic.approach:
1. stringstream ss(s).
2. while getline(ss, tok, '.').
3. stoi(tok).
logic.code:
stringstream ss(s); string tok; vector<int> parts;
while (getline(ss, tok, '.')) parts.push_back(stoi(tok));

lessons.title: 011. deque
lessons.notes:
Double-ended queue: push_front, push_back, pop_front, pop_back all O(1).
Random access v[i] works, O(1).
Insert in the middle is O(n).
Used for sliding window maximum and 0-1 BFS.

logic.problem: Maximum of every window of size k.
logic.thinking: Smaller items before a bigger one can never be the answer.
logic.logic: Keep indexes with decreasing values.
logic.approach:
1. Pop back while smaller.
2. Push the index.
3. Pop front if out of the window.

lessons.title: 012. list and forward_list
lessons.notes:
list: doubly linked, insert/erase O(1) with an iterator.
No v[i]; use iterators.
splice moves nodes without copying; sort() and unique() are members.
forward_list is singly linked and uses less memory.

logic.problem: Move an item to the front in O(1).
logic.thinking: A vector would shift every element.
logic.logic: Splice a node to the front.
logic.approach:
1. Keep a map key → list iterator.
2. On use: l.splice(l.begin(), l, it).
3. On overflow: l.pop_back().

lessons.title: 013. pair and tuple
lessons.notes:
pair<int,int> p = {a, b}; p.first, p.second; make_pair.
Pairs compare by first, then second.
tuple<int,int,int> t; get<0>(t); tie(a, b, c) = t.
Structured bindings: auto [x, y] = p.

logic.problem: Sort items by one value and keep the label.
logic.thinking: Pairs sort by the first element.
logic.logic: Put the sort key first.
logic.approach:
1. Make pair(key, label).
2. sort.
3. Read the pairs.

lessons.title: 014. bitset
lessons.notes:
bitset<N> b: fixed-size array of bits.
set, reset, flip, test, count, any, none, to_string.
Operators & | ^ ~ << >> work on whole bitsets.
Great for sieve and subset flags.

logic.problem: Mark primes up to n with little memory.
logic.thinking: One bit per number is enough.
logic.logic: Cross out multiples.
logic.approach:
1. Set all bits.
2. For each prime, reset its multiples.
3. Count the set bits.

lessons.title: 015. stack
lessons.notes:
push, pop, top, size, empty. LIFO, all O(1).
pop() returns nothing; read top() first.
Check empty() before top().
Monotonic stack: next greater element.

logic.problem: Days until a warmer temperature.
logic.thinking: Compare each day with unresolved earlier days.
logic.logic: Pop days that just found their answer.
logic.approach:
1. Stack of indexes.
2. While today > top, pop and fill the answer.
3. Push today.

lessons.title: 016. queue
lessons.notes:
push, pop, front, back, size, empty. FIFO, all O(1).
pop() returns nothing; read front() first.
BFS is built on a queue.
Queue of pairs for (node, distance).

logic.problem: Rot all oranges and count minutes.
logic.thinking: All rotten oranges spread at the same time.
logic.logic: Push all sources first.
logic.approach:
1. Push every rotten orange.
2. Process level by level.
3. Count levels.

lessons.title: 017. priority_queue
lessons.notes:
Max-heap by default; min-heap: priority_queue<int, vector<int>, greater<int>>.
push, pop O(log n), top O(1).
Pairs compare by first, then second.
Custom order: a struct with operator(), or a lambda.
No iteration, no update of an element.

logic.problem: Find the k largest elements.
logic.thinking: You only need k items, not a full order.
logic.logic: Keep the k best; pop the smallest.
logic.approach:
1. Push each item.
2. If size > k, pop.
3. The heap holds the answer.
logic.code:
priority_queue<int, vector<int>, greater<int>> pq;
for (int x : a) { pq.push(x); if ((int)pq.size() > k) pq.pop(); }

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in An Array

lessons.title: 018. set
lessons.notes:
Sorted, unique elements; insert, erase, find, count in O(log n).
begin() is the minimum, prev(end()) is the maximum.
lower_bound(x) = first element ≥ x; upper_bound(x) = first element > x.
Iterate in sorted order.

logic.problem: Find the next larger value that was inserted before.
logic.thinking: A sorted set answers neighbour questions fast.
logic.logic: lower_bound jumps to the neighbour.
logic.approach:
1. Insert values.
2. auto it = s.lower_bound(x).
3. Check it and prev(it).

lessons.title: 019. multiset
lessons.notes:
Sorted, duplicates allowed.
erase(value) removes all copies; erase(iterator) removes one.
count(x), find(x), lower_bound, upper_bound.
Great for sliding-window median and order statistics.

logic.problem: Remove one copy of a value.
logic.thinking: erase(value) deletes every copy.
logic.logic: Use find, then erase the iterator.
logic.approach:
1. auto it = ms.find(x).
2. If it != end, ms.erase(it).
logic.code:
multiset<int> ms = {2, 2, 3};
ms.erase(ms.find(2));

lessons.title: 020. map
lessons.notes:
Sorted by key; O(log n) operations.
m[key] creates the key with a default value.
find(key), count(key), erase(key), at(key).
Iterate with for (auto& [k, v] : m).
lower_bound on keys works like set.

logic.problem: Group words that are anagrams.
logic.thinking: Anagrams share the same sorted letters.
logic.logic: Use the sorted word as the key.
logic.approach:
1. key = sorted(word).
2. m[key].push_back(word).
3. Output all groups.
logic.code:
map<string, vector<string>> m;
for (auto& w : words) { string k = w; sort(k.begin(), k.end()); m[k].push_back(w); }

lessons.title: 021. multimap
lessons.notes:
Sorted map with duplicate keys.
No operator[]; use insert and equal_range.
equal_range(key) gives all values for a key.
Often replaced by map<key, vector<value>>.

logic.problem: Store several values under one key in sorted order.
logic.thinking: A key can repeat.
logic.logic: Use equal_range to read them.
logic.approach:
1. mm.insert({k, v}).
2. auto [a, b] = mm.equal_range(k).
3. Loop a to b.

lessons.title: 022. unordered_set
lessons.notes:
Hash set: insert, erase, find, count in O(1) average.
No order.
reserve(n) avoids rehashing.
Worst case O(n) with many collisions.

logic.problem: Detect a repeated value fast.
logic.thinking: You only need membership, not order.
logic.logic: Insert and check in one step.
logic.approach:
1. Insert each value.
2. If insert fails, it was seen.
3. Stop or count.
logic.code:
unordered_set<int> seen;
if (!seen.insert(x).second) cout << "duplicate";

lessons.title: 023. unordered_map and Hashing
lessons.notes:
Hash map: O(1) average.
m[x]++ is the standard frequency counter.
Use find to read without creating keys.
Anti-hash tests can slow it in contests; add a custom hash or use map.
reserve and max_load_factor help speed.

logic.problem: Count subarrays with sum k.
logic.thinking: pre[j] - pre[i] = k means the subarray sums to k.
logic.logic: Look up pre - k among earlier prefixes.

lessons.title: 024. Ordered Containers: Bounds and Tricks
lessons.notes:
lower_bound(x): first ≥ x. upper_bound(x): first > x.
Predecessor: step back from lower_bound. Successor: upper_bound.
Erase while iterating: it = s.erase(it).
set.count in a loop is O(log n) each; store the result.

logic.problem: Find the closest value to x in a set.
logic.thinking: The neighbours of x are the two items around lower_bound.
logic.logic: Check lower_bound and the one before it.
logic.approach:
1. it = s.lower_bound(x).
2. Candidate 1: *it.
3. Candidate 2: *prev(it).

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

lessons.title: 025. sort and Custom Comparators
lessons.notes:
sort(first, last) is O(n log n), not stable.
Descending: sort(v.rbegin(), v.rend()) or greater<int>().
A comparator must be a strict weak ordering: return a < b, never a <= b.
Sort by several keys: compare the first, then break ties.

logic.problem: Sort intervals by start, then by end.
logic.thinking: A comparator tells which item comes first.
logic.logic: Return true when a must come before b.
logic.approach:
1. Write a lambda.
2. Compare the main key.
3. Break ties with the next key.

lessons.title: 026. stable_sort, partial_sort and nth_element
lessons.notes:
stable_sort keeps the order of equal items.
partial_sort(first, mid, last) sorts only the smallest k.
nth_element puts the k-th item in place in O(n) average.
is_sorted checks order.

logic.problem: Find the median without a full sort.
logic.thinking: Only one position needs to be correct.
logic.logic: nth_element partitions around position k.
logic.approach:
1. k = n / 2.
2. nth_element(begin, begin + k, end).
3. Read a[k].
logic.code:
nth_element(a.begin(), a.begin() + k, a.end());
int kth = a[k];

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in An Array

lessons.title: 027. binary_search, lower_bound, upper_bound
lessons.notes:
These work on sorted ranges in O(log n).
binary_search returns true or false.
lower_bound = first ≥ x. upper_bound = first > x.
Count of x = upper_bound - lower_bound. equal_range gives both.
Index = it - v.begin().

logic.problem: Find the first and last position of x.
logic.thinking: First position = lower_bound; end = upper_bound.
logic.logic: Use the two iterators as the range.
logic.approach:
1. lo = lower_bound(x).
2. hi = upper_bound(x).
3. If lo == hi, x is missing.

problems.title: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array

lessons.title: 028. reverse, rotate, swap, fill and iota
lessons.notes:
reverse(first, last) reverses a range.
rotate(first, mid, last) makes mid the new first.
swap(a, b), fill(first, last, x), iota(first, last, start) fills 0, 1, 2…
All of these work on any container with iterators.

logic.problem: Rotate an array right by k.
logic.thinking: Rotation is a move of the middle pointer.
logic.logic: Rotate left by n - k equals rotate right by k.
logic.approach:
1. k %= n.
2. rotate(begin, begin + n - k, end).

lessons.title: 029. min, max, minmax and Element Finders
lessons.notes:
min(a, b), max(a, b), minmax(a, b), clamp(x, lo, hi).
min({a, b, c}) takes an initializer list.
min_element and max_element return iterators.
Index: it - v.begin().

logic.problem: Where is the maximum element?
logic.thinking: The algorithm returns an iterator, not a value.
logic.logic: Convert it to an index.
logic.approach:
1. auto it = max_element(begin, end).
2. value = *it.
3. index = it - begin.
logic.code:
auto it = max_element(v.begin(), v.end());
int value = *it, idx = it - v.begin();

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array

lessons.title: 030. accumulate, partial_sum, adjacent_difference
lessons.notes:
accumulate(first, last, init) sums a range. Use 0LL for long long.
partial_sum builds a prefix-sum array.
adjacent_difference is the opposite: differences of neighbours.
Pass a function as a fourth argument for a custom operation.

logic.problem: Build the prefix sums in one call.
logic.thinking: Prefix sums are a running total.
logic.logic: partial_sum writes the running total.
logic.approach:
1. vector<long long> p(n).
2. partial_sum(a.begin(), a.end(), p.begin()).
3. Sum(l, r) = p[r] - p[l-1].

lessons.title: 031. count, find and Predicates
lessons.notes:
count(first, last, x), count_if(first, last, pred).
find(first, last, x) and find_if return an iterator or end().
any_of, all_of, none_of return bool.
Use a lambda as the predicate.

logic.problem: Is every element positive?
logic.thinking: all_of checks the condition for every item.
logic.logic: Write the condition as a lambda.
logic.approach:
1. pred = [](int x){ return x > 0; }.
2. all_of(begin, end, pred).
logic.code:
bool ok = all_of(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x > 0; });
int evens = count_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x % 2 == 0; });

problems.title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in An Array

lessons.title: 032. unique, remove and the Erase-Remove Idiom
lessons.notes:
unique removes consecutive duplicates; sort first.
remove and remove_if move kept items forward and return the new end.
They do not shrink the vector; call erase.
Erase-remove: v.erase(remove(v.begin(), v.end(), x), v.end()).
C++20: erase(v, x) and erase_if.

logic.problem: Delete all copies of x from a vector.
logic.thinking: remove only moves items; erase cuts the tail.
logic.logic: Remove first, then erase the tail.
logic.approach:
1. it = remove(begin, end, x).
2. v.erase(it, v.end()).

lessons.title: 033. next_permutation and prev_permutation
lessons.notes:
next_permutation rearranges to the next larger order and returns false at the end.
Start from a sorted range to visit all permutations.
Duplicates are handled: each distinct order appears once.
prev_permutation goes the other way.

logic.problem: List all permutations of an array.
logic.thinking: A sorted start, then step through.
logic.logic: do-while with next_permutation.
logic.approach:
1. sort(a).
2. do { use a } while (next_permutation(a)).
logic.code:
sort(a.begin(), a.end());
do { res.push_back(a); } while (next_permutation(a.begin(), a.end()));

lessons.title: 034. merge and Set Algorithms
lessons.notes:
merge combines two sorted ranges into a third.
set_union, set_intersection, set_difference, set_symmetric_difference need sorted input.
includes checks whether one sorted range contains another.
Results go to an output iterator: back_inserter(res).

logic.problem: Intersection of two sorted arrays.
logic.thinking: Both ranges are sorted, so the algorithm can scan once.
logic.logic: Write results with back_inserter.
logic.approach:
1. Sort both.
2. set_intersection(..., back_inserter(res)).
logic.code:
vector<int> res;
set_intersection(a.begin(), a.end(), b.begin(), b.end(), back_inserter(res));

lessons.title: 035. Heap Algorithms
lessons.notes:
make_heap, push_heap, pop_heap, sort_heap work on a plain vector.
Max-heap by default; pass greater<> for a min-heap.
push_heap after push_back; pop_heap then pop_back.
Handy when you need to see all elements of the heap.

logic.problem: Use a heap stored in a vector.
logic.thinking: You can inspect and change the vector between operations.
logic.logic: Keep the heap property with the helper calls.
logic.approach:
1. make_heap(v).
2. Push: push_back, push_heap.
3. Pop: pop_heap, pop_back.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream

lessons.title: 036. transform, for_each, copy, replace and generate
lessons.notes:
transform(first, last, out, f) applies f to each item.
for_each(first, last, f) runs f on each item.
copy, copy_if, replace, replace_if, generate, fill_n.
back_inserter(v) appends to a vector.

logic.problem: Square every number.
logic.thinking: The same operation applies to each element.
logic.logic: transform with a lambda.
logic.approach:
1. Make an output vector.
2. transform(a.begin(), a.end(), out.begin(), f).
logic.code:
vector<int> sq(n);
transform(a.begin(), a.end(), sq.begin(), [](int x) { return x * x; });

lessons.title: 037. Numeric Utilities
lessons.notes:
gcd(a, b) and lcm(a, b) from <numeric> (C++17).
__gcd(a, b) works in older GCC.
__builtin_popcount(x), __builtin_clz(x), __builtin_ctz(x); add ll for long long.
abs, pow, sqrt, ceil, floor from <cmath>; prefer integers when possible.

logic.problem: Count the set bits of a number.
logic.thinking: Hardware has a single instruction for this.
logic.logic: Use popcount.
logic.approach:
1. cnt = __builtin_popcount(x).
2. Power of two means cnt == 1.

lessons.title: 038. Lambdas with STL
lessons.notes:
[capture](params) { body }.
[&] captures by reference, [=] by copy, [x] one variable.
Use with sort, find_if, transform, priority_queue.
Recursive lambda: auto f = [&](auto self, int x) -> int { ... }; f(f, n).
mutable lets a copy-capture change.

logic.problem: Sort numbers by frequency, then by value.
logic.thinking: The order depends on a map the lambda must see.
logic.logic: Capture the frequency map by reference.
logic.approach:
1. Count frequencies.
2. sort with [&](int a, int b).
3. Compare cnt[a], then a.

lessons.title: 039. Functors and Comparators
lessons.notes:
A functor is a struct with operator().
Built in: less<>, greater<>, plus<>, multiplies<>.
Use a functor as the third template argument of set, map or priority_queue.
A comparator must be a strict weak ordering.

logic.problem: Order a priority_queue by a custom rule.
logic.thinking: Container order is part of its type.
logic.logic: Pass a struct as the third parameter.
logic.approach:
1. struct Cmp { bool operator()(A a, A b) }.
2. priority_queue<A, vector<A>, Cmp>.

problems.title: Kth Smallest Element in a Sorted Matrix
Find K Pairs with Smallest Sums

lessons.title: 040. Custom Hash for pair and tuple Keys
lessons.notes:
unordered_map<pair<int,int>, T> does not compile without a hash.
Write a struct with operator() and combine the hashes.
Alternative: encode the pair into a long long key (x * M + y).
Or use map<pair<int,int>, T> at O(log n).

logic.problem: Use a coordinate as a map key.
logic.thinking: A pair has no default hash.
logic.logic: Combine the two hashes.
logic.approach:
1. Write struct H.
2. Pass it to unordered_map.
3. Or encode to long long.

lessons.title: 041. Iterator Invalidation and Common Bugs
lessons.notes:
vector: push_back or insert may invalidate all iterators; erase invalidates from the position on.
map/set/list: erase invalidates only the erased iterator.
Use it = c.erase(it) while looping.
Common bugs: unsigned size() - 1, m[key] creating keys, a comparator with <=, using end() as a value.

logic.problem: Erase items while looping.
logic.thinking: Erasing changes the container under your iterator.
logic.logic: Use the iterator returned by erase.
logic.approach:
1. Loop with an explicit iterator.
2. If erasing: it = erase(it).
3. Else ++it.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array II

lessons.title: 042. Performance: reserve, emplace, move
lessons.notes:
reserve(n) avoids repeated reallocation.
emplace_back constructs in place; push_back copies or moves.
Pass large objects by const&; use auto& in range-for.
std::move transfers ownership instead of copying.
ios::sync_with_stdio(false) and "\n" speed up I/O.

logic.problem: Why is my copy-heavy loop slow?
logic.thinking: for (auto x : v) copies every element.
logic.logic: Use references.
logic.approach:
1. for (const auto& x : v).
2. reserve before many push_backs.
3. Use emplace_back.

lessons.title: 043. Policy-based Ordered Set (pb_ds)
lessons.notes:
GCC only: #include <ext/pb_ds/assoc_container.hpp>.
ordered_set supports order_of_key(x) and find_by_order(k) in O(log n).
Replace less with less_equal for multiset-like behaviour.
Not available on every judge or in MSVC.

logic.problem: Count how many inserted values are smaller than x.
logic.thinking: A normal set cannot give ranks.
logic.logic: order_of_key counts smaller keys.
logic.approach:
1. Insert values.
2. smaller = os.order_of_key(x).
3. kth = *os.find_by_order(k).

problems.title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self

lessons.title: 044. Random Numbers and Shuffle
lessons.notes:
mt19937 rng(seed) is a good generator.
uniform_int_distribution<int> d(lo, hi).
shuffle(first, last, rng) permutes a range.
Seed with chrono::steady_clock::now().time_since_epoch().count().

logic.problem: Shuffle an array fairly.
logic.thinking: Every permutation must be equally likely.
logic.logic: Use shuffle with a good engine.
logic.approach:
1. Make the engine.
2. shuffle(v.begin(), v.end(), rng).

lessons.title: 045. Choosing the Right Container
lessons.notes:
Need order or neighbours: set / map.
Need only membership or count: unordered_set / unordered_map.
Need min or max repeatedly: priority_queue.
Need both ends: deque. Need LIFO: stack. Need FIFO: queue.
Need O(1) random access: vector.
Need stable references and O(1) splice: list.

logic.problem: Support insert, delete and random pick in O(1).
logic.thinking: A hash map finds items; a vector picks randomly.
logic.logic: Map value → index in a vector.
logic.approach:
1. Append to the vector and store the index.
2. Delete: swap with last, pop.
3. Pick a random index.
logic.code:
vector<int> v; unordered_map<int,int> pos;
void ins(int x) { pos[x] = v.size(); v.push_back(x); }

lessons.title: 046. Grids and 2D Containers
lessons.notes:
vector<vector<int>> for grids; vector<string> for character maps.
Directions: int dx[] = {1,-1,0,0}, dy[] = {0,0,1,-1}.
Bounds check before access.
visited as a grid of the same size.
queue<pair<int,int>> for BFS.

logic.problem: Count islands in a grid.
logic.thinking: Each island is one connected group.
logic.logic: Visit a land cell, then sink all connected land.
logic.approach:
1. Scan cells.
2. On land, count + 1 and flood.
3. Flood marks cells visited.

lessons.title: 047. Graphs with STL
lessons.notes:
vector<vector<int>> g(n) is an adjacency list.
BFS with queue, DFS with recursion or stack.
Dijkstra: priority_queue<pair<int,int>, vector<pair<int,int>>, greater<>>.
Topological sort with a queue and an indegree array.

logic.problem: Shortest path in a weighted graph.
logic.thinking: BFS counts edges, but edges have weights.
logic.logic: Always expand the closest unsettled node.
logic.approach:
1. dist = INF, dist[s] = 0.
2. Pop the smallest (d, u).
3. Relax each edge.

lessons.title: 048. Intervals and Scheduling with STL
lessons.notes:
Sort by start to merge; sort by end for the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals.
map<int,int> can store disjoint intervals; lower_bound finds neighbours.
multiset or priority_queue tracks end times (meeting rooms).
Always define whether touching intervals overlap.

logic.problem: Merge overlapping intervals.
logic.thinking: After sorting by start, overlaps are neighbours.
logic.logic: Extend the last interval or start a new one.
logic.approach:
1. Sort by start.
2. If start <= last end, extend.
3. Else push a new interval.

lessons.title: 049. Top Interview Patterns with STL
lessons.notes:
Frequency map + heap for top-k.
Deque for sliding-window maximum.
Set or map for neighbour queries.
Sort + two pointers for pair problems.
Stack for next greater and parentheses.
Know which container each pattern uses.

logic.problem: Top k frequent elements.
logic.thinking: Count first, then keep the k best counts.
logic.logic: Count with unordered_map, select with a min-heap.
logic.approach:
1. Count with unordered_map.
2. Push (count, value) to a min-heap.
3. Keep size k.

lessons.title: 050. Final STL Cheat Sheet and Practice Plan
lessons.notes:
Keep a one-page list: container → operations → complexity.
Practise in rounds: containers, then algorithms, then mixed problems.
After each problem write which STL tools you used.
Time yourself: 20 minutes for an easy, 40 for a medium.
Review mistakes weekly.

logic.problem: Which STL tools does this problem need?
logic.thinking: The statement hints at the container.
logic.logic: Name the operations, then the container.
logic.approach:
1. Write the operations needed.
2. Pick the container.
3. Pick the algorithms.
